# Test data factory rules (Python, factory_boy)

Apply these rules whenever you create or use a factory in a Python test.

## Always apply (critical, high)

### Set every value the test asserts on explicitly when you build test data

_high · any_

**Rule.** Build test data from a builder or factory, and pass an explicit override for every field the test
asserts on or branches on. Leave random values only in fields the test never looks at. Use named
variants (traits) for whole states such as "admin" or "inactive" instead of repeating the same
overrides in many tests.

**Why.** An assertion against a randomly generated value passes or fails depending on the seed, and a
reader cannot tell from the test which value matters. An explicit override documents the input the
test depends on and makes the failure reproducible.

### Pass asserted values as keyword arguments and model states as Traits

_high · python, factory-boy_

**Rule.** Pass every value the test asserts on as a keyword argument to the factory call. Use
`build_batch(size, **kwargs)` for lists. Define recurring states as `factory.Trait` in the
factory's `class Params` and switch them on with `admin=True`.

**Why.** A Faker-generated name asserted in a test passes only by coincidence of the seed, and the reader
cannot see which input the test depends on.

**Incorrect:**

```python
user = UserFactory.build()
assert render_greeting(user) == f"Hello, {user.name}"
```

**Correct:**

```python
class UserFactory(factory.Factory):
    class Meta:
        model = User

    name = factory.Faker("name")
    role = "member"

    class Params:
        admin = factory.Trait(role="admin")


user = UserFactory.build(name="Ada Lovelace")
admins = UserFactory.build_batch(3, admin=True)
assert render_greeting(user) == "Hello, Ada Lovelace"
```
